name: Delta Electronics
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Delta Electronics is the volume leader in AI server power — #1 global power supply vendor (WAWT), reported at over half of AI-server AC/DC supply (CommonWealth) with brokerage estimates above 60% — and AI data-center power plus cooling crossed 50% of company revenue for the first time in Q2 2026, a quarter that printed record revenue NT$183.2B (+48%) and H1 EPS (NT$17.59) already above any prior full year. BACKGROUND: Founded 1971 by Bruce Cheng; chairman/CEO Ping Cheng; four segments (Power Electronics, Infrastructure, Automation, Mobility) with Power Electronics + Infrastructure now 87% of sales. The 800 VDC portfolio is the deepest published: 660 kW in-row power racks with 480 kW of embedded BBU, 18.5 kW PSUs at 98%, solid-state transformers at 98.5%, supercapacitor shelves, SiC e-fuses, and 3 MW CDUs now shipping. FY2025 revenue NT$554.9B (+32%), net income +71%. Capex guided to NT$70B (+50%) for 2026; a reported $2B SiC supply deal with Infineon underpins the 800V ramp. Thai-listed subsidiary DELTA TH is Thailand's largest listed company.
ecosystemRole: We assess Delta as the incumbent standard inside the NVIDIA rack — the first-qualified power-shelf supplier for GB200/GB300 NVL72 and TrendForce's named primary beneficiary of the 800V HVDC shift — making it the direct competitive ceiling for Megmeet, LITEON, and every rack-power challenger in this file. Basis: qualified supplier sets reported as Delta first, LITEON and Megmeet behind; the only vendor publishing a complete grid-to-chip 800 VDC stack (SST through DC-DC brick through liquid-cooled busbar); and Goldman-attributed modeling that 800 VDC raises BOM-per-watt ~43% with Delta capturing the largest share. The contested variable is the new sidecar power-rack segment, where Chinese press reports Megmeet displacing LITEON at #2 and holding first-mover position — the sharpest supplier fight in the AIDC power chain.

productsAndServices.name: 800 VDC rack power (In-Row Power Racks, power shelves, PSUs)
productsAndServices.description: Flagship 800 VDC In-Row 660 kW Power Rack (GTC 2026): six 110 kW power shelves each embedding an 80 kW BBU (480 kW BBU per rack), built on 18.5 kW AC/DC PSUs at up to 98% efficiency with energy-storage aluminum capacitors buffering GPU load distortion; 1RU 90 kW DC/DC shelves (800V→50V, 98.5%); earlier 1.1 MW-scale in-row configurations from 106 kW HVDC shelves; ±400 VDC line scalable to 2.4 MW; ORv3 72 kW shelves; HVDC Power Capacitance (supercap) shelves up to 10 s backup; SiC e-fuse with <3 µs fault cutoff; liquid-cooled 50 VDC/8,000 A busbar.
productsAndServices.positioning: The deepest 800 VDC catalog published by any vendor; mass production of ±400V from Q3 2026, 800V small-volume Q4 2026 with the true ramp in 2027. Delta holds a reported exclusive on NVIDIA DC-DC modules.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Into the NVIDIA MGX ODM/OEM ecosystem and directly to hyperscalers/CSPs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Rubin Ultra (~600 kW) and Feynman-class (1 MW) racks drive per-rack content up; Goldman-attributed modeling has DC/DC converters alone reaching ~14% of revenue at >40% operating margins by 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Solid-state transformer & microgrid stack
productsAndServices.description: SST converting medium-voltage AC directly to 800 VDC at up to 98.5% efficiency; Energy Variance Appliance rack for peak-to-average smoothing (97% full-load); solid-oxide fuel cell line (60% electrical efficiency, world-first FPSO application; Centrica off-grid data-center project); ESS at 2.5 MW/5 MWh per pair of 20-ft containers; company claim of >4% grid-to-chip efficiency gain (to ~92%) from the 800V architecture.
productsAndServices.positioning: Delta and GE Vernova are the two vendors pairing SSTs with complete AI-factory power architectures — Delta from the rack up, GEV from the grid down.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Solutions projects with hyperscalers and campus developers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: SST commercialization rides the same 2027 800V volume ramp.

productsAndServices.name: Liquid cooling (GoCool CDUs, cold plates)
productsAndServices.description: GoCool 3 MW liquid-to-liquid CDU officially shipping to AI data centers (1.5 LPM/kW, scalable to eight-unit groups); 2.4 MW 800VDC-native CDU with N+1 hot-swappable 25 kW HVDC pumps and 4°C approach; in-rack 4U 140 kW (GB300 NVL72-certified) and 6U 250 kW units; 300 kW liquid-to-air retrofit CDU; Vera Rubin NVL72 cold plates; liquid cooling was >12% of revenue in Q2 2026 (from ~9-10%).
productsAndServices.positioning: The only rack-power leader that is simultaneously a top-tier CDU vendor — power and cooling sold as one architecture, mirroring (from the component side) what Vertiv/Schneider sell from the facility side.
productsAndServices.roadmap: CDU capacity scaling with the Blackwell→Rubin transition; 2.4 MW unit is 800VDC-native by design.

productsAndServices.name: Data-center infrastructure (InfraSuite, UPS, prefab)
productsAndServices.description: Ultron DPM Gen-2 UPS (250-2,500 kVA, 97.5% double-conversion, SiC, scalable to 20 MW N+1); UZR3 lithium battery cabinets (>3 GW deployed globally; NFPA 855 large-scale fire tested); claimed >6.5 GW of UPS capacity across US data centers; Prefabricated AI Modular Data Center (Computex 2026) cutting deployment time up to 60%, integrating 800VDC in-row power and 3 MW cooling.
productsAndServices.positioning: Puts Delta in direct facility-level competition with Vertiv, Eaton, and Schneider — from the opposite direction: a components giant moving up-stack rather than a facilities incumbent moving down.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Data-center infrastructure channel (Delta Americas; Infrastructure segment).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Infrastructure segment revenue grew 82% in FY2025 with segment profit +413% — the fastest-scaling business in the company.

productsAndServices.name: Legacy platform (industrial automation, EV, components)
productsAndServices.description: Industrial automation (drives, servos, PLCs — NT$54.9B FY2025), Mobility/EV (OBCs, DC-DC, motor controllers — loss-making at -NT$1.19B in FY2025), passive components, networking (1.6T/800G switches for GPU fabrics), fans and thermal components.
productsAndServices.positioning: The diversified base that funded the AI pivot; automation and EV now dilute rather than drive growth.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mobility restructuring continues; automation cycling with Chinese industrial demand.

recentDevelopments.read: Securing the semiconductor input that gates every 98%+ efficiency claim in the DC-power stack. (Reported by trade press; not company-confirmed in detail.)

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Delta's AI-power leadership is real, current, and structurally advantaged into the 800V generation. Basis: #1 power-supply vendor globally (WAWT), first-qualified across GB200/GB300 shelf sets, the reported NVIDIA DC-DC exclusive, the deepest published 800 VDC stack, and a reported $2B SiC supply lock with Infineon; TrendForce independently names Delta the primary 800V beneficiary.

(High confidence) We assess the margin narrative has peaked in the near term. Basis: management's own guidance that H2 2026 gross margins will not exceed ~35.6% (versus Q1's record 37.0%), the 3-year AI-equipment depreciation change, memory/MOSFET cost inflation described as 'fully constrained,' and Q4 2025's 0.7pp gross-margin miss showing consensus already prices aggressive margins.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the sidecar power-rack segment is the one field where Delta's dominance is genuinely contested. Basis: Chinese-press reporting that Megmeet displaced LITEON as the #2 NVL72 shelf supplier and holds first-mover position in the power-rack segment Morgan Stanley sizes at >RMB30B for 2026; Delta was pressed on Megmeet, Vertiv, and Flex by analysts on its own Q2 call. Unverified precision, but directionally corroborated across sources.

(Moderate confidence) We assess customer and architecture concentration is the structural risk the diversification no longer offsets. Basis: AI data center >50% of revenue concentrates exposure on NVIDIA rack cadence and a handful of hyperscalers (NVIDIA's own top-2 customers were 39% of its revenue); no third-party source quantifies NVIDIA as a share of Delta revenue — itself a transparency gap.

(Low confidence) We assess the valuation dispersion signals genuine disagreement rather than consensus conviction. Basis: sell-side targets span NT$1,330 to NT$4,500 (the top being a secondary-sourced Goldman figure), DCF-style fair values sit ~45% below market, and the Goldman 2028 model runs ~95% above consensus EPS — the widest bull-bear spread among the incumbents in this file.
